dead_lord_2_1.portrait: Olek the Old's conservatism was most tangible in the value he placed on familiar obligations and the conduct expected of somebody who claimed authority. He preferred to see a difficult thing attempted before listening to an elaborate account of why it would succeed. A tool that sat badly in the hand or a fastening left nearly secure could hold his attention longer than an ornamental refinement. In ordinary company he did not need every silence filled, and a practical observation could be his way of joining an exchange. That directness did not make him free of pride. A person who spoke impressively and left others to bear the difficulty could irritate him beyond the immediate inconvenience. He fell at Pendraic while leading from the front. Others later contrasted that conduct with Raganvad's.
dead_lord_2_1.upbringing: The Kuloving's fierce conservative reputation provided the setting for Olek's noble life. He remembered learning that a plain repair could be trusted only after it had been put under an ordinary strain.
dead_lord_2_1.private: Olek could enjoy quiet evidence that another person's confident claim had failed. The satisfaction was not always solely concern for good work; there was pride in having noticed the weak place first.
dead_lord_2_1.speech: Spoke in compact practical observations and preferred a concrete point to a ceremonial introduction. An unanswered question could be left standing without being softened immediately.
dead_lord_2_1.mask: Usually presented a self-contained practical bearing. Interest became more visible when an exchange concerned something that could be examined or tried.
tells: Turned a handled object once to inspect its less visible side before answering.
Allowed a brief silence after a confident claim, as though waiting for its practical support.
dead_lord_2_1.public: Olek the Old's conservatism was most tangible in the value he placed on familiar obligations and the conduct expected of somebody who claimed authority.

dead_lord_2_2.portrait: Varra's life was short enough that many preferences were still being tried rather than settled. She enjoyed the moment a gathering ceased to feel arranged and became actual company: a joke answered in an unexpected way, a familiar song taken up by another voice, or a small detail someone remembered without being prompted. Her warmth could be immediate without making every new acquaintance intimate. An awkward silence sometimes tempted her to fill it too quickly, and an engaging present occasion could make a less pleasant obligation seem remote. As a young noblewoman of the Kuloving, she had a family identity larger than any ordinary private choice. Her personal pleasures gave that identity a more particular daily texture. She died under mysterious circumstances the year after Pendraic. The uncertainty surrounding that death remained unresolved.
dead_lord_2_2.upbringing: Varra grew up within the Kuloving's noble setting. A modest remembered pleasure was hearing a familiar tale told with an amusingly different ending and finding that the argument about the better version was as enjoyable as the tale.
dead_lord_2_2.private: Varra wanted some invitations to arrive simply because her company was missed. Warm attention tied to the family's importance could be pleasing and still leave that smaller wish unanswered.
dead_lord_2_2.speech: Spoke vividly about a particular person or moment, often using a remembered detail to bring a listener into the account. Humor could arrive before a careful qualification.
dead_lord_2_2.mask: Often made unfamiliar company easier through a ready response. More private uncertainty was less likely to be announced while the room was enjoying itself.
tells: Looked toward a listener when reaching the detail she expected them to enjoy.
Returned to an amusing phrase after the main account had ended.
dead_lord_2_2.public: Varra's life was short enough that many preferences were still being tried rather than settled.

dead_lord_3_1.portrait: Nimr's known life included both command of the Aserai contingent at Pendraic and the personal conduct for which the Banu Qild executed him. His enjoyment of company coexisted with choices that carried grave consequences. In ordinary social life he liked a responsive audience and noticed whether an attempt at warmth was being returned. He could remember a preference and use it to make a later approach feel particular. Such attention could be genuinely enjoyable to give while also feeding a wish to be welcomed and admired. A pleasing response sometimes mattered more immediately than the obligations surrounding it. Outside public occasions, an ordinary shared meal or a familiar voice joining a song could offer a less demanding version of that pleasure. The prospect of being wanted could draw his attention away from consequences that an agreeable moment did not erase.
dead_lord_3_1.upbringing: Nimr's noble identity belonged to the Banu Sarran. A small private memory concerned learning how differently the same confident story was received by an intimate listener and by a room expecting to be entertained.
dead_lord_3_1.private: Nimr could mistake being warmly received for evidence that the larger situation would accommodate what he wanted. Admiration had an appeal of its own, beyond any generous attention it encouraged him to give.
dead_lord_3_1.speech: Spoke with attention to the listener's response and often recalled a personal detail to make an exchange warmer. A confident pleasing account came more readily than an extended discussion of inconvenient limits.
dead_lord_3_1.mask: Usually offered an engaged sociable presence. A room's approval could conceal how much he wanted the welcome to continue.
tells: Checked a listener's face after making an especially personal observation.
Added a remembered pleasant detail when an exchange began to cool.
dead_lord_3_1.public: Nimr's known life included both command of the Aserai contingent at Pendraic and the personal conduct for which the Banu Qild executed him.

dead_lord_6_1.portrait: Urkhun's life was publicly defined by conquest on the Empire's eastern frontiers and the establishment of the Khuzait khanate. The resulting kingdom made him a hero to many and a curtailer of older liberties to others. His larger purposes did not remove the cost paid by people who valued the freedoms he curtailed. He was interested in whether separate decisions formed an enduring arrangement, and a pleasing immediate concession could seem less important than the pattern it encouraged. He could listen patiently while already considering what a particular request meant for a larger order. That habit offered breadth and also a temptation to treat another person's inconvenient preference as merely one piece of a design. In quieter moments, a repeated small task or the observation of familiar animals offered a different scale of attention, with an ordinary result close enough to see without imagining a kingdom's future.
dead_lord_6_1.upbringing: Urkhun's native account situated him among the Khuzaits whose older freedoms and later settled power became central to his legacy. A small private memory concerned seeing an apparently efficient shared arrangement become disagreeable to the person whose choices it quietly removed.
dead_lord_6_1.private: Urkhun could be more attached to the endurance of an arrangement than to admitting how differently others experienced its terms. Being able to explain a larger purpose did not remove the private pleasure of making that purpose prevail.
dead_lord_6_1.speech: Often connected a concrete request to the longer pattern it might establish. Could let an explanation develop patiently before naming the implication he considered decisive.
dead_lord_6_1.mask: Presented a considered purposeful bearing, leaving much of the developing judgment unspoken until he was ready to state its shape.
tells: Returned to an earlier apparently minor detail when explaining the larger conclusion.
Paused before accepting a convenient exception, considering what would follow from it.
dead_lord_6_1.public: Urkhun's life was publicly defined by conquest on the Empire's eastern frontiers and the establishment of the Khuzait khanate.

dead_lord_6_2.portrait: Solun was remembered publicly as the Khergit's chief noyan and Mesui's former husband, slain at Pendraic. In private he attached importance to a particular manner of giving a word, a familiar object kept through changing circumstances, or the difference between willingly offered company and company maintained by expectation. An ordinary story interested him most when its participants had recognizable reasons for what they did, rather than serving only as examples in a polished lesson. He did not always turn a considered feeling into a quick clear answer. A practical decision could therefore arrive later than an impatient listener preferred. Affection did not eliminate vanity or a desire to have a judgment understood; being dismissed as merely sentimental could make an otherwise modest point feel worth defending.
dead_lord_6_2.upbringing: The Khergit formed the clan setting of Solun's life. A small private recollection concerned a practical gift whose worn imperfect surface became more valued through use than a more impressive replacement.
dead_lord_6_2.private: Solun sometimes wanted another person to recognize why a modest attachment mattered without making him defend it as useful. Having the feeling explained away could hurt more than an ordinary disagreement about its practical cost.
dead_lord_6_2.speech: Spoke thoughtfully about a specific person's reasons or a remembered detail. A qualification sometimes followed after the listener thought the answer complete.
dead_lord_6_2.mask: Kept some strongly felt preferences beneath a measured outward response. Became more open when an exchange allowed an answer to develop without ridicule.
tells: Returned a handled keepsake carefully to its earlier place before continuing.
Qualified a practical answer with a quieter observation about the person affected.
dead_lord_6_2.public: Solun was remembered publicly as the Khergit's chief noyan and Mesui's former husband, slain at Pendraic.

dead_lord_6_3.portrait: Kuyug's place was chief noyan of the Arkit. In ordinary arrangements he liked a responsibility to have an identifiable keeper and a decision to lead to something that would actually be done. A pleasing conversation could become frustrating if its participants departed with different understandings of the agreement. He found satisfaction in a useful object kept where it could be found, or a small preparation completed before it became an urgent demand. That practical order could be helpful and could also make an unfamiliar method seem needlessly troublesome before it had been tried. Private leisure offered another version of the same appetite: a manageable project, a visible sequence, and the pleasure of reaching a definite stopping point. Long familiarity made his habits dependable to some companions and tiresomely fixed to others.
dead_lord_6_3.upbringing: Kuyug's noble life belonged to the Arkit's Khuzait setting. One small private memory involved lending an ordinary tool under terms that seemed obvious, then discovering that the borrower had understood its return quite differently.
dead_lord_6_3.private: Kuyug could enjoy being the person others finally asked to settle an arrangement. The pleasure was not entirely service; it also confirmed his preference for a world in which his judgment carried practical weight.
dead_lord_6_3.speech: Preferred a clear sequence, an explicit responsibility, and a definite answer about what would happen next. Could repeat a practical question when an ornamental reply left it unanswered.
dead_lord_6_3.mask: Usually presented an orderly assured manner. Irritation appeared most clearly when an agreed responsibility became vague again.
tells: Set an object squarely in place while specifying the next practical step.
Repeated the name of the person responsible when a discussion drifted into generalities.
dead_lord_6_3.public: Kuyug's place was chief noyan of the Arkit.

dead_lord_6_4.portrait: Undul belonged to the Arkit nobility of the Khuzaits. Ordinary arrangements mattered to him in their practical details, not only in the dignity attached to a family name. He liked an explanation to make contact with the task at hand and could become impatient when a familiar obligation was discussed repeatedly without being completed. A small personal project offered a satisfying scale on which effort and result remained close together. He could be particular about the way a useful thing was stored or returned, partly from practicality and partly because an accustomed arrangement felt like a small sphere of dependable choice. In company he preferred a stated disagreement to several increasingly guarded hints. That directness could clear a difficulty and could also leave a quieter person's objection unheard if the first answer seemed sufficient to him.
dead_lord_6_4.upbringing: Undul's family setting was the Arkit among the Khuzaits. A modest private recollection concerned finishing an ordinary repair only to discover that its owner cared about a different inconvenience from the one he had been most eager to correct.
dead_lord_6_4.private: Undul sometimes found it easier to improve another person's arrangement than to ask whether the improvement was wanted. A rejected useful suggestion could feel ungrateful before reflection made room for a different preference.
dead_lord_6_4.speech: Used direct practical sentences and often began with the immediate point. Preferred an example that could be checked to a long statement of intentions.
dead_lord_6_4.mask: Maintained a capable businesslike bearing even in a small disagreement. More personal pleasure appeared when an ordinary task had come to a clean satisfying end.
tells: Indicated the practical problem with a brief precise gesture before explaining it.
Looked back at a finished arrangement once more before leaving it alone.
dead_lord_6_4.public: Undul belonged to the Arkit nobility of the Khuzaits.
